style: Late-90s Brooklyn mafioso rap, a crime-film rulebook read aloud, 90 BPM, dim and minimal. Lead voice: a big heavyset Brooklyn boss, cavernous chest-deep baritone, round and thick, a faint asthmatic wheeze, slow audible inhales before each rule, lazy unhurried conversational flow that drags late into the pocket, cool menace, half-amused, volume level and low the whole time like a man who has never needed to shout. Beat: grimy New York street-corner hip hop from a dusty sampler, a lone eerie Rhodes-style minor-key jazz chord phrase repeating, fat thudding kick, snare that cracks like a slammed door, closed hats, deep upright bass notes, hiss and crackle, saturated cassette warmth, narrow mono mix, vocal dry, close and loud. Each number is a turntable scratch of a gruff barked count. Rules only: no hook, no chorus, no singing.
exclude: trap, 808 rolls, rattling hi-hats, autotune, melodic singing, sung chorus, choir, glossy modern mix, EDM, synth pads, thin high voice, yelling, double-time flow, west coast g-funk
lyrics:
[Intro: low, unbothered, a slow breath first]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: barked count "One!"]
[Verse: lazy, late, calm menace]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: barked count "Two!"]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: barked count "Three!"]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: music cuts, just the voice, quiet threat]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
title: tec-r2-mafioso-menace
